comparator.route: Ordinary Rechtsgeleerdheid bachelor with first-listed year-two and year-three restricted options
comparator.sourceNotes: The official current prospective 2027–28 year overviews reconcile to 60+60+60=180 EC. Year one is common to the law bachelors; year two has 55 EC compulsory public/criminal-law and professional/research courses plus one restricted 5-EC choice, instantiated as first-listed Arbeidsrecht. Year three has 47 EC compulsory private/corporate/EU law, moot-court work and a 5-EC bachelor thesis; one restricted 4-EC private-law option is Huurrecht, one restricted 4-EC integration option is AI en recht, and the first-listed 5-EC meta-legal choice is criminology 4 EC together with its matching essay 1 EC. The choices are one coherent neutral instance, not universally compulsory subjects. The year-one zero-credit Tutoraat is excluded. The programme has no ordinary reserved exchange semester. The pages are prospective and show concurrent year cohorts, not a guaranteed single-entrant schedule.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad law/public institutions programme is the closest defensible interdisciplinary UCR response. Private-law and business interests support a substantially distinct second curriculum. A proposed third public-law or justice-philosophy alternative would largely rearrange the already-used seven UCR law courses with nearby politics and sociology, and the available catalogue does not support a third independently coherent Dutch-law sequence.

notes.text: UCR teaches general/comparative private, criminal, constitutional, international, EU and human-rights law alongside political, business and social study. Radboud requires a much denser Dutch public and civil-law curriculum, procedure, simulated court practice and a legal bachelor thesis. UCR study is not a Dutch Rechtsgeleerdheid law qualification and does not establish access to regulated legal professions.
